note: Pick the case (stage 6); w or na? and iść or jechać? (level extras A1). Imperfective or perfective? comes with A2 extras; chodzić / jeździć and the prefixed verbs extend the going tree from A2 on.

trees.title: Pick the case
trees.intro: Think of one noun in your sentence and answer the questions about it.

start.question: Is there a preposition right before the noun (or before its adjective)?
start.help: Prepositions are short words such as do, z, w, na, bez, dla, u.

options.label: Yes, there is a preposition
No preposition
do, od, bez, dla, u, obok, koło
options.why: These prepositions always take the genitive.

options.label: z
na
w
przez, or za meaning in … time (za tydzień)
options.why: przez and za meaning in … time take the accusative. (za meaning behind takes the instrumental: za domem.)

example.en: I'm coming back in a week.

options.label: o, po, przy (about, after, next to)
options.why: o, po and przy usually take the locative: mówić o filmie, po lekcji, przy oknie. (o meaning for, as in prosić o, takes the accusative, and so does po meaning to fetch: Idę po chleb.)

options.label: przed, pod, nad, między (in front of, under, above, between)
options.why: When they say where something is, these prepositions take the instrumental. (Going under or in front of something takes the accusative: Kot wchodzi pod stół.)

example.en: I'm waiting in front of the house.

options.label: from, out of (Where from?)
options.why: z meaning from takes the genitive.

options.label: with, together with (With whom? With what?)
options.why: z meaning with takes the instrumental.

na.question: Does na say where something goes, or where it is?

options.label: Where it goes (Where to?)
options.why: na + accusative = where to.

options.label: Where it is (Where?)
options.why: na + locative = where.

options.label: Where something is (Where?)
options.why: w + locative = where: in a building, a town, a country.

options.label: Where someone goes: into a building, a town, a country
options.why: Going into a place usually takes do + genitive, not w: Idę do szkoły, not Idę w szkołę.

options.label: A day of the week (on Monday …)
options.why: w + a day of the week takes the accusative. (Months and years take the locative: w maju.)

options.label: A month or a year (in May, in 2025)
options.why: w + a month or a year takes the locative.

example.en: I have a holiday in May.

role.question: What does the noun do in the sentence?

options.label: It is the subject: the person or thing that does the action
options.why: The subject is in the nominative. (After quantity words like dużo or pięć it goes into the genitive: Pięć osób czeka.)

options.label: It comes after to jest or to są
options.why: After to jest / to są the noun stays in the nominative.

options.label: It is a noun after być saying who someone is (a job, a nationality, a role)
options.why: być + noun takes the instrumental: Jestem lekarzem. With a first name in an introduction the nominative is usual: Jestem Tomek. An adjective after być stays in the nominative: Kawa jest gorąca.

options.label: It is the object of the verb: the person or thing the action goes to
It says whose something is, or follows a quantity word (dużo, mało, pięć …)
options.why: Possession and quantities take the genitive.

example.en: I have a lot of work.

options.label: It is the person who receives something (To whom?)
options.why: The receiver of a gift, a message or help is in the dative.

options.label: It is a tool or a means of transport (With what? By what?)
options.why: Tools and means of transport without a preposition take the instrumental.

options.label: You are speaking to someone directly
options.why: Addressing someone takes the vocative.

object.question: Which kind of verb is it?
object.help: A few verbs take another case for their object. Check them first.

options.label: szukać, słuchać, potrzebować, używać, bać się
options.why: These verbs take the genitive, also in a positive sentence.

options.label: pomagać, dziękować, or the person after dawać (komu?)
options.why: The person you help, thank or give something to is in the dative, also after nie. The thing you give stays in the accusative: Daję mamie kwiaty.

options.label: Another verb (mieć, lubić, kupować, czytać …)

negation.question: Is the verb negated with nie?

options.label: Yes, there is nie before the verb
options.why: After nie the direct object switches from the accusative to the genitive.

options.label: No, the sentence is positive
options.why: Most verbs take a direct object in the accusative.

example.en: I'm buying a newspaper and coffee.

trees.title: w or na?
trees.intro: For a place: which little word do you need, and which case follows it?

start.question: What kind of place is it?

options.label: Most buildings, rooms and shops: sklep, bank, szkoła, kino, kuchnia

answer.title: w
answer.text: Most buildings and rooms take w. Where you are: w + locative. Where you go: do + genitive.

options.label: A town, a city or a country

answer.title: w
answer.text: Towns and most countries take w. Where you are: w + locative. Where you go: do + genitive.

options.label: Home

answer.title: w domu / do domu
answer.text: dom takes -u in both: w domu (at home), do domu (home, when you go there).

options.label: A na-place (poczta, dworzec, lotnisko, uniwersytet), a stop, a square, a street, a surface or an event
poczta, dworzec, przystanek, rynek, lotnisko, uniwersytet

answer.title: na
answer.text: These places take na. Learn them as a list. Where you are: na + locative. Where you go: na + accusative.

options.label: An event or a meal: a concert, a lesson, a coffee

answer.title: na
answer.text: Events take na. Where you are: na + locative. Where you go: na + accusative.

options.label: A surface or a street: a table, a shelf, a street

answer.title: na
answer.text: On a surface or in a street: na + locative.

examples.en: The phone is on the table.
The car is in the street.

trees.title: iść or jechać?
trees.intro: English "go" is two verbs in Polish. Answer one question about the trip.

options.label: On foot
By car, bus, tram, train or bike

answer.title: jechać
answer.text: With a vehicle: jechać (jadę, jedziesz, jadą). The vehicle is in the instrumental, with no preposition (a bike: rowerem or na rowerze).

examples.en: I'm taking the bus to the centre.

options.label: The sentence doesn't say how
Somewhere in town: work, school, the shop, the cinema

answer.title: iść
answer.text: In town iść is usual for everyday places such as work, school or the cinema.

examples.en: The children are going to school.

options.label: To another town or another country

answer.title: jechać
answer.text: Another town means a vehicle, so jechać.

examples.en: In July we're going to England.
